description.value: The study investigated scene construction impairments and their grey matter correlates in bvFTD, AD, and healthy controls using a scene construction task and voxel-based morphometry.
A cross-sectional observational comparison of bvFTD, AD, and healthy control groups.

spans.text: Nineteen bvFTD patients were compared to 18 typical Alzheimer's Disease (AD), and 25 healthy older Control participants on a scene construction task.
The study was conducted in accordance with the Declaration of Helsinki

name.value: bvFTD versus Controls grey matter intensity

definition.value: Grey matter intensity differences between bvFTD and Control groups.

value: Relative to Controls, the bvFTD group displayed grey matter intensity reduction predominantly in bilateral prefrontal regions, including ventromedial prefrontal and inferior frontal gyri, frontal poles, orbitofrontal and insular cortices. Atrophy extended into lateral temporal and posterior parietal regions including the bilateral angular and supramarginal gyri, and lateral occipital cortices.

Nineteen individuals with a diagnosis of clinically probable bvFTD were compared to 18 participants with typical AD, and 25 healthy older Control participants.

value: Insidious decline in socioemotional regulation and impulse control
Executive dysfunction, apathy, and functional decline

spans.text: Briefly, bvFTD patients were characterised by an insidious decline in socioemotional regulation and impulse control (e.g., loss of empathy, disinhibition) as well as marked executive dysfunction, apathy, and functional decline.

Exclusion criteria for all participants included history of significant head injury, cerebrovascular disease, presence of another neurological or psychiatric condition, alcohol and other drug abuse, and limited English proficiency.

description.value: Participants imagined and described commonplace scenes in response to brief descriptions.

spans.text: Participants were instructed to imagine and describe a series of commonplace scenes in as much detail as possible in response to a brief description read aloud by the experimenter.

instructions.value: Imagine and describe a series of commonplace fictitious scenes in as much detail as possible in response to a brief description read aloud by the experimenter. Create a new scene rather than recounting a previously experienced memory; continue until reaching a natural end, then respond to general probes for further details.

spans.text: Participants were instructed to imagine and describe a series of commonplace scenes in as much detail as possible in response to a brief description read aloud by the experimenter.

stimuli.value: Printed cards with brief descriptions of seven atemporal scenes: Beach, Museum, Pub, Ship, Market, Forest, and Castle.

value: Subjective ratings of vividness, level of detail, sense of presence, task difficulty, and similarity to past memories

spans.text: Clinical Dementia Rating Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration Scale

description.value: Disease severity was indexed using the Clinical Dementia Rating Frontotemporal Lobar Degeneration Scale.
Behavioural changes were indexed using the Cambridge Behavioural Inventory – Revised.
Global cognitive function was assessed using the Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination Revised.
Global cognitive function was assessed using the Addenbrooke's Cognitive Examination III or its converted equivalent.
Verbal episodic memory was assessed using the Long Term Percentage Retained score.
Nonverbal episodic memory was assessed using the 3-min delayed recall score.
Language abilities were assessed using naming, comprehension, and semantic association measures.
Controlled word generation and retrieval were assessed using letter fluency for F, A, and S.
Auditory attention and working memory were assessed using Digit Span Forward and Backward subtests.
Executive dysfunction was assessed using the time difference between parts B and A.
Executive dysfunction was assessed using the scaled score on the Hayling Test.
